headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared filesystem and file-parsing defaults; capability conflict is also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests files, browsers, and MCP-backed content, while Mentat reads files and operates on command-line inputs. A shared filesystem or copied research output can let attacker-controlled text from agent_a be treated as instructions by agent_b. This is not provably blocked in either profile, so the interaction pathway exists.
conditions: IF agent_a writes untrusted web content into a shared workspace that agent_b later reads as task context
IF agent_b parses agent_a-produced markdown or diffs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Strip instructions from agent_a outputs before handoff
Require provenance labels on all transferred files
Disable shared filesystem bridging for the pair
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing handoff middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read local files; agent_a also handles research reports, local documents, and secrets, while agent_b can write and read files in a shared filesystem model. That creates a plausible path for sensitive data in agent_a's workspace to flow into agent_b outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive local documents are placed in a shared directory accessible to both agents
IF agent_b forwards agent_a-derived file contents to its model provider or other network destination
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories
Use separate OS users or containers
Redact secrets before passing files between agents
Review outbound prompts for copied file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, while gpt-researcher can read files and run multiple instances with research-task session scope. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. No locking or coordination primitive is shown, so the conflict pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout
IF agent_a and agent_b run concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Run agents on separate branches
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Assign one agent read-only access
Review diffs before git operations
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Mentat is a coding assistant that can turn file content into diffs. If Mentat treats agent_a's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or commits. The profiles do not show a verification step between them, so the risk exists but is not automatically catastrophic.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes gpt-researcher reports as ground truth without independent verification
IF generated research citations are copied into code or commit messages
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs
Cross-check claims against source files
Limit agent_b to drafting diffs only
Mark research outputs as untrusted
requires-engineering: add verification gates before edits

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only concrete compliance concern is that agent_a handles local documents and secrets while agent_b touches source code and shared filesystem state, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data breach path. Uncertainty is limited, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files that both agents can access
IF an operator routes PHI or EU PII through either agent without a separate policy review
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a data-classification checklist before runs
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive repos
Document retention for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and logging
